To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
galaxies with the same stellar mass have very different stellar mass distributions, which are the result of different star formation histories and/or different merger histories.

(1) the local stellar mass-size relation is tight, (2) the stellar mass concentration of galaxies is correlated with total stellar mass, and (3) the stellar mass surface density at a given distance from the galaxy center is correlated with total mass.
the stellar mass surface density of a galaxy is a strong predictor of its central concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How do galaxies form, and what determines the stellar mass and sizes of their components?
the study of stellar mass distributions in galaxies and how they relate to other properties of these systems.
the stellar structure of nearby galaxies, and we have made the data products that are needed to explore this topic available to the community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Spitzer Survey of the Stellar Structure of Galaxies (S4G) has provided a wealth of data on the distribution of the stellar mass in nearby, well-resolved, galaxies, and it has set the stage for future work on this topic.
the S4G data products are a unique and invaluable resource to the community.
S4G is the largest, deepest, and highest-quality survey of nearby galaxies ever conducted at these wavelengths.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the S4G survey has provided a detailed census of stellar mass distribution in the local universe.

the S4G data products provide the community with an accurate, homogeneous, and extensive database of structural parameters for nearby galaxies, and the S4G stellar masses are among the most robust and precise estimates available for galaxies in the local universe.
we have produced a homogeneous and accurate data set for a large sample of nearby galaxies, which will be useful for a wide range of scientific studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stellar mass–size and mass–concentration relations are remarkably tight, with the scatter in the former being ~0.1 dex.
galaxies with the same stellar mass can exhibit a wide range in central stellar mass concentration.
the stellar mass surface density profiles of galaxies can vary significantly, and this variation is correlated with their total stellar mass.
